newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says petrochems sell-off goes on-TV.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says petrochems sell-off goes on-TV.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister, Guillermo Ortiz, said on Wednesday the sell-off of the country's 61 secondary petrochemical plants would continue despite recent set-backs to the proposed privatisation, a TV network reported.
Televisa quoted Ortiz in an interview in Washington as saying that the sell-off was going on.

Members of Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, known by its Spanish initials as PRI, voted at a recent convention to write into statutes that the party wanted to keep state control over oil, gas, and oil derivatives industries.
The PRI has legislative majorities and could block the government move.
The sell-off has also faced other stiff opposition, delaying the start of the process. Winners of the first ammonia complex on the block should have been named in April.

Numerous sectors see it as a threat to the sovereignty that Mexico jealously guards on state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), with articles in the Mexican constitution governing Pemex operations. Pemex currently runs the petrochemical plants.
